# Postgres: Customize Auto-Generated Field Names

## Introduction

Hasura auto-generates GraphQL field names based on your database table and column names. If you'd like to change the
defaults, it is possible to override and rename the auto-generated table and column field names exposed over the GraphQL
API.

:::tip Supported from

This feature is supported in versions `v1.0.0-beta.8` and later.

:::

## Expose columns with a different name in the GraphQL API

<Tabs groupId="user-preference" className="api-tabs">
<TabItem value="console" label="Console">

Head to the `Data -> [table-name] -> Modify`. On the relevant field, click `Edit` and change the GraphQL field name to a
name of your choice.

<Thumbnail src="/img/schema/custom-field-name-column.png" alt="Customize GraphQL field name" />

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="cli" label="CLI">

You can customize auto-generated field names in the `tables.yaml` file inside the `metadata` directory:

```yaml {4-6}
- table:
    schema: public
    name: author
  configuration:
    column_config:
      addr:
        custom_name: address
```

Apply the Metadata by running:

```bash
hasura metadata apply
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="api" label="API">

A custom field name can be set for a column via the following 2 methods:

1.  passing a [Table Config](/api-reference/syntax-defs.mdx#table-config) with the
    [ColumnConfig](/api-reference/syntax-defs.mdx#columnconfig) to the
    [pg_track_table](/api-reference/metadata-api/table-view.mdx#metadata-pg-track-table) API while tracking a table:

    ```http
    POST /v1/metadata HTTP/1.1
    Content-Type: application/json
    X-Hasura-Role: admin

    {
      "type": "pg_track_table",
      "args": {
        "source": "<db_name>",
        "table": "author",
        "configuration": {
          "column_config": {
            "addr": {
              "custom_name": "address"
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
    ```

2.  using the
    [pg_set_table_customization](/api-reference/metadata-api/table-view.mdx#metadata-pg-set-table-customization) API to
    set the [ColumnConfig](/api-reference/syntax-defs.mdx#columnconfig):

    ```http
    POST /v1/metadata HTTP/1.1
    Content-Type: application/json
    X-Hasura-Role: admin

    {
      "type": "pg_set_table_customization",
      "args": {
        "source": "<db_name>",
        "table": "author",
        "column_config": {
          "addr": {
            "custom_name": "address"
          }
        }
      }
    }
    ```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Expose a table with a different name in the GraphQL API

By default, the GraphQL type of a table and all the names generated from it use the table name. For example, a table
called `author_details` gives you an `author_details` type, `author_details_bool_exp` and `author_details_insert_input`
input types and root fields such as `author_details`, `author_details_by_pk` and `insert_author_details`.

You can replace the table name in all of them at once by setting the `custom_name` of the table. With `custom_name` set
to `author`, the same table gives you an `author` type, `author_bool_exp` and `author_insert_input` input types and
`author`, `author_by_pk` and `insert_author` root fields. Root fields that you have
[customized individually](#expose-table-root-fields-with-a-different-name-in-the-graphql-api) keep their custom names.

<Tabs groupId="user-preference" className="api-tabs">
<TabItem value="cli" label="CLI">

You can set a custom name for a table in the `tables.yaml` file inside the `metadata` directory:

```yaml {4-5}
- table:
    schema: public
    name: author_details
  configuration:
    custom_name: author
```

Apply the Metadata by running:

```bash
hasura metadata apply
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="api" label="API">

A custom name can be set for a table by passing a [Table Config](/api-reference/syntax-defs.mdx#table-config) with
`custom_name` to the [pg_track_table](/api-reference/metadata-api/table-view.mdx#metadata-pg-track-table) API while
tracking a table, or to the
[pg_set_table_customization](/api-reference/metadata-api/table-view.mdx#metadata-pg-set-table-customization) API for a
table that is already tracked:

```http
POST /v1/metadata HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
X-Hasura-Role: admin

{
  "type": "pg_set_table_customization",
  "args": {
    "source": "<db_name>",
    "table": "author_details",
    "configuration": {
      "custom_name": "author"
    }
  }
}
```

`pg_set_table_customization` replaces the existing customization of the table, so include any `custom_root_fields` and
`column_config` that you want to keep in the same `configuration`.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Expose table root fields with a different name in the GraphQL API

<Tabs groupId="user-preference" className="api-tabs">
<TabItem value="console" label="Console">

Head to the `Data -> [table-name] -> Modify`. Click the `Edit` button in the `Custom GraphQL Root Fields` section and
define names over which you'd like to expose the table root fields.

<Thumbnail src="/img/schema/custom-field-name-root-fields.png" alt="Customize GraphQL root field" />

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="cli" label="CLI">

You can expose table root fields with a different name in the GraphQL API in the `tables.yaml` file inside the
`metadata` directory:

```yaml {4-7}
- table:
    schema: public
    name: author
  configuration:
    custom_root_fields:
      select_by_pk: author
      select: authors
```

After that, apply the Metadata by running:

```bash
hasura metadata apply
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="api" label="API">

A custom field name can be set for a table root field via the following 2 methods:

1.  passing a [Table Config](/api-reference/syntax-defs.mdx#table-config) with the
    [Custom Root Fields](/api-reference/syntax-defs.mdx#custom-root-fields) names to the
    [pg_track_table](/api-reference/metadata-api/table-view.mdx#metadata-pg-track-table) API while tracking a table:

    ```http
    POST /v1/metadata HTTP/1.1
    Content-Type: application/json
    X-Hasura-Role: admin

    {
      "type": "pg_track_table",
      "args": {
        "source": "<db_name>",
        "table": "author",
        "configuration": {
          "custom_root_fields": {
            "select": "authors",
            "select_by_pk": "author"
          }
        }
      }
    }
    ```

2.  using the
    [pg_set_table_customization](/api-reference/metadata-api/table-view.mdx#metadata-pg-set-table-customization)
    Metadata API to set the [Custom Root Fields](/api-reference/syntax-defs.mdx#custom-root-fields) names

    ```http
    POST /v1/metadata HTTP/1.1
    Content-Type: application/json
    X-Hasura-Role: admin

    {
      "type": "pg_set_table_customization",
      "args": {
        "source": "<db_name>",
        "table": "author",
        "custom_root_fields": {
            "select": "authors",
            "select_by_pk": "author"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>
